1. Heard the parties.

2. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Session Trial Case No. 556 of 2018 arising out of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017 involving the offences punishable under Amrita Banerjee @ Amrita Austine Okaro vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5633575/

sentences.text: This criminal miscellaneous petition has also been filed with a prayer to quash the order taking cognizance dated 16.02.2018 by which cognizance has been taken under Section 420/120B/406/366/498/34 of the Indian Penal Code and also to quash the order dated 28.09.2018 by which the record of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017, S.T. No. 566 of 2018 has been committed to the Court of Sessions.

3. The allegation against the petitioners is that the petitioners in furtherance of their common intention, taking advantage of the weak mental condition of the wife of the complainant took her to their house and induced her to institute case against the complainant and the mental condition of the wife of the complainant was not sound.
The wife of the complainant was having an A.T.M. Card and by the time she was with the petitioners, Rs.1,48,000/- was withdrawn from the bank account.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners are innocent and they have been falsely implicated in this case.
The case has been instituted with an ulterior motive to harass and humiliate the petitioners.
It is next submitted that there is no allegation of abduction of the wife of the complainant by the petitioners or the petitioners having cheated anybody.
It is then submitted that the wife of the complainant was never in fact kidnapped and she is a Senior Doctor of Anesthesia, working with the Central Government, E.S.I. Hospital, Jamshedpur.

It is next submitted that since the conjugal life of the complainant with his wife is not good as the complainant is having extra marital affair with a woman and stays with her at Dhanbad where he is posted in connection with his job, hence he is claiming that his wife is mentally ill.

The wife of the complainant filed a complaint case against the complainant and his family members involving the offence punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code; in which the petitioner no.1 has been mentioned as a witness and the petitioner no.2 is the husband of the petitioner no.1 and for wrecking vengeance upon the petitioners, this false case has been foisted.

It is next submitted that the wife of the complainant has filed M.T.S. No. 708 of 2017 for a decree of divorce against the complainant and as the petitioners are helping the wife of the complainant namely Dr. Madia Sanga, hence this false case has been foisted against the petitioners.

It is next submitted that the complaint is not even supported by affidavit as has been opined by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Priyanka Srivastava & Anr. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors., reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287 para -30 & 31 of which reads as under:-
"30.

entities.text: Priyanka Srivastava & Anr. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors., reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In our considered opinion, a stage has come in this country where Section 156(3)
CrPC applications are to be supported by an affidavit duly sworn by the applicant who seeks the invocation of the jurisdiction of the Magistrate.
That apart, in an appropriate case, the learned Magistrate would be well advised to verify the truth and also can verify the veracity of the allegations.
This affidavit can make the applicant more responsible.
We are compelled to say so as such kind of applications are being filed in a routine manner without taking any responsibility whatsoever only to harass certain persons.

That apart, it becomes more disturbing and alarming when one tries to pick up people who are passing orders under a statutory provision which can be challenged under the framework of the said Act or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

But it cannot be done to take undue advantage in a criminal Amrita Banerjee @ Amrita Austine Okaro vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5633575/
2 court as if somebody is determined to settle the scores.
31.

sentences.text: We have already indicated that there has to be prior applications under Sections 154(1) and 154(3) while filing a petition under Section 156(3).
Both the aspects should be clearly spelt out in the application and necessary documents to that effect shall be filed.

The warrant for giving a direction that an application under Section 156(3) be supported by an affidavit is so that the person making the application should be conscious and also endeavour to see that no false affidavit is made.
It is because once an affidavit is found to be false, he will be liable for prosecution in accordance with law.
This will deter him to casually invoke the authority of the Magistrate under Section 156(3).
That apart, we have already stated that the veracity of the same can also be verified by the learned Magistrate, regard being had to the nature of allegations of the case.

We are compelled to say so as a number of cases pertaining to fiscal sphere, matrimonial dispute/family disputes, commercial offences, medical negligence cases, corruption cases and the cases where there is abnormal delay/laches in initiating criminal prosecution, as are illustrated in Lalita Kumari [(2014) 2 SCC 1 : (2014) 1 SCC (Cri) 524] are being filed.
That apart, the learned Magistrate would also be aware of the delay in lodging of the FIR."
and thus the continuation of the criminal proceeding will amount to abuse of process of court.

5. Hence, it is submitted that the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Session Trial Case No. 556 of 2018 arising out of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017 including the order taking cognizance dated 16.02.2018 and order dated 28.09.2018 by which the record of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017, S.T. No. 566 of 2018 has been committed to the Court of Sessions be quashed and set aside.
6.

The learned Addl. P.P. however objects to the prayer for quashing the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Session Trial Case No. 556 of 2018 arising out of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017 including the order taking cognizance dated 16.02.2018 and order dated 28.09.2018 by which the record of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017, S.T. No. 566 of 2018 has been committed to the Court of Sessions and submitted that the statement on solemn affirmation of the complainant and the statement of the inquiry witness makes out the offence for which the learned Magistrate has found prima facie case.
Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

7. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, it is crystal clear that there is no allegation against the petitioners of cheating anybody nor there is any allegation against the petitioners of dishonestly misappropriating any property entrusted to them, in fact there is no allegation of entrustment of any property to the petitioners.

There is no allegation against the petitioners of abducting the wife of the complainant or compelling to marry her with anybody nor there is any allegation of enticing away the wife of the complainant with the intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person or having concealing or detained her with such intent; hence, the offence punishable under Section 498 of the Indian Penal Amrita Banerjee @ Amrita Austine Okaro vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5633575/
3 Code is also not made out.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thus even if the complaint, the statement of the complainant on solemn affirmation and the statement of the inquiry witnesses are taken to be true in its entirety, still the none of the offence punishable under Section 120/406/366/498/34 of the Indian Penal Code or for that matter under Section 120B of the Indian penal Code is not made out against the petitioners.

8. Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that the continuation of the criminal proceeding against the petitioners will amount to abuse of process of court and this is a fit case where in the interest of justice the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Session Trial Case No. 556 of 2018 arising out of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017 including the order taking cognizance dated 16.02.2018 and order dated 28.09.2018 by which the record of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017, S.T. No. 566 of 2018 has been committed to the Court of Sessions be quashed and set aside.

9. Accordingly, the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Session Trial Case No. 556 of 2018 arising out of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017 including the order taking cognizance dated 16.02.2018 and order dated 28.09.2018 by which the record of Complaint Case No. 4279 of 2017,
S.T. No. 566 of 2018 has been committed to the Court of Sessions is quashed and set aside.

10. In the result, this criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed.
11.
In view of disposal of this criminal miscellaneous petition, the interim order granted earlier stands vacated.
